evidence.quote: product or service consumed by residents of this state

summary.short: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act: adds Chapter 541 to the Business & Commerce Code, giving Texas consumers rights over their personal data and imposing duties on controllers and processors that conduct business in Texas or produce products consumed by its residents. Enforced by the attorney general; in force from July 1, 2024.
summary.long: Adds Chapter 541 (Consumer Data Protection) to the Business & Commerce Code. It applies to persons that conduct business in Texas or produce products or services consumed by Texas residents, excluding state agencies, financial institutions, HIPAA-covered entities, nonprofits, higher education institutions and certain electric utilities; small businesses are excluded except for a consent rule on sales of sensitive data. Consumers may confirm, access, correct, delete, port and opt out of targeted advertising, data sales and certain profiling. Controllers must respond to requests within 45 days, provide an appeal process, offer two or more request methods, limit collection, secure data, and obtain consent for sensitive data, and must post privacy notices, with sale notices for sensitive or biometric data. Processors act under controller contracts. Controllers must assess processing for targeted advertising, sales, risky profiling and sensitive data. The attorney general has exclusive enforcement authority and may issue civil investigative demands; a written notice and 30-day opportunity to cure apply before action, and violations carry civil penalties of up to $7,500 each. No private right of action is created, and local ordinances are preempted. Chapter 541 takes effect July 1, 2024, with one provision effective January 1, 2025.

notes: Text is H.B. 4 as enacted (88th Leg., R.S.); the approval and governor signature dates are blank, so no enactment date is stated. Chapter 541 is added by Section 2; Section 3(d) expires September 1, 2025; Section 541.055(e) takes effect January 1, 2025 and the rest on July 1, 2024 (Section 7). Section 541.156 states there is no private right of action; Section 541.155 sets a civil penalty not to exceed $7,500 per violation. thresholds.measurement: share of outstanding voting securities held by the company, or control over director elections or management
thresholds.consequence: An entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another entity is its affiliate; affiliates are excluded from the definition of third party and from the definition of sale.

thresholds.value_text: an individual younger than 13 years of age
thresholds.measurement: age of the individual; for known children, a controller's actual knowledge of or wilful disregard of the child's age (Sec. 541.001(17))
thresholds.consequence: Individual is a child; personal data collected from a known child is sensitive data, and processing it requires consent or compliance with COPPA.
thresholds.conditions: Known child requires that the controller has actual knowledge of, or wilfully disregards, the child's age.

evidence.quote: "Child" means an individual younger than 13 years

thresholds.variable_text: radius of precision for precise geolocation data (feet)
thresholds.measurement: precision and accuracy with which the data directly identifies the specific location of an individual
thresholds.consequence: Location data meeting this precision is precise geolocation data, which is included in sensitive data.
thresholds.conditions: Data must be derived from technology, such as GPS-level latitude and longitude or other mechanisms; the term excludes communication content and data from advanced utility metering infrastructure or utility equipment.

enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of Chapter 541 after the cure period in Sec. 541.154, or breach of a written statement provided to the attorney general under that section; also sale of sensitive data without prior consent by a small business person under Sec. 541.107(a), which is subject to the penalty under Sec. 541.155 (Sec. 541.107(b))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: An amount not to exceed $7,500 for each violation
enforcement.penalty_formula: Per violation; the attorney general may also recover reasonable attorney's fees and other reasonable expenses incurred in investigating and bringing an action (Sec. 541.155(c))
enforcement.cure_period: The attorney general must notify the person in writing not later than the 30th day before bringing the action; no action if the person cures within the 30-day period and provides a written statement (Sec. 541.154)
